primary_objective: tree structural entropy H^T; lower is better

claims.claim: The weighted rooted-NNI delta equals the two-cross-weight closed form.
claims.evidence: Random weighted graphs and binary trees; compare every predicted delta with full H^T recomputation.
claims.falsifier: Any mismatch above 1e-9 after ruling out floating-point accumulation.

claims.claim: One-step and compound NNI never worsen their input; the compatibility variant never worsens the identical se_hier initializer.
claims.evidence: Unit tests, per-run monotonic endpoint checks, and exact full-objective verification.
claims.falsifier: Any committed endpoint greater than its paired input beyond 1e-10.

claims.claim: NNI closes a reproducible local-optimality gap left by current hierarchy constructors.
claims.evidence: Paired refinement of se_hier, official HCSE/BBM, Paris, and SE-agglomerative outputs on 50 frozen HSBM graphs and four real networks.
claims.falsifier: No positive one-step or compound gaps outside the fixed trap witness.

claims.claim: Bounded compound NNI escapes cases where strict one-NNI descent stalls.
claims.evidence: Fixed exact witness plus 30/50 additional gains after multi-start one-step descent.
claims.falsifier: Compound search adds cost without improving any non-constructed case.

claims.claim: The enhanced optimizer improves the practical entropy/runtime frontier.
claims.evidence: H^T and planted dendrogram purity with 95% confidence intervals; traced benchmark runtime plus clean size scaling.
claims.falsifier: Lower H^T requires prohibitive runtime or degrades hierarchy recovery consistently.

scaling: HSBM n=32,64,96,128 with three seeds per size

baselines: HypCSE (related continuous feature-to-tree method; not a fixed-graph discrete baseline)
statistics: Paired per-graph comparisons; report mean, 95% t interval, raw records, and deterministic artifact verifiers.
